title: Approximation of a local map into a completed stalk
statement: Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth], let $X,Y$ be schemes locally of finite type over $S$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $x\in X$, $y\in Y$ lie over $s\in S$. Assume that $\mathcal O_{S,s}$ is a G-ring [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]. Let $\theta:\mathcal O_{Y,y}\to\widehat{\mathcal O}_{X,x}$ be a local $\mathcal O_{S,s}$-algebra homomorphism, where the completion is at the maximal ideal [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. For every integer $N\geq1$, there are an etale morphism $p:U\to X$ [def-weil-etale-morphism], a point $u\in U$ with $p(u)=x$ such that $\kappa(x)\to\kappa(u)$ is an isomorphism [def-weil-residue-field], and an $S$-morphism $f:U\to Y$ with $f(u)=y$, such that for every $a\in\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ the elements $\widehat p^{\sharp}(\theta(a))$ and $\iota_u(f_u^{\sharp}(a))$ differ by an element of $\mathfrak m_u^N\widehat{\mathcal O}_{U,u}$. Here $\widehat p^{\sharp}:\widehat{\mathcal O}_{X,x}\to\widehat{\mathcal O}_{U,u}$ is the map on maximal-adic completions induced by $p$, $\iota_u:\mathcal O_{U,u}\to\widehat{\mathcal O}_{U,u}$ is the completion map, and $\mathfrak m_u$ is the maximal ideal of $\mathcal O_{U,u}$.

source.place: Tag 0CAU, lemma-map-approximation, statement and proof at lines 11017–11068; Artin approximation input is Smoothing Ring Maps Tag 0CAR, lemma-approximation-property-variant.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-local-map-affine-chart-dictionary] to choose actual affine open charts $S_0=\operatorname{Spec}R$, $X_0=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $Y_0=\operatorname{Spec}B$, their marked primes $\mathfrak r,\mathfrak p,\mathfrak q$, and a finite presentation $B=R[T_1,\ldots,T_n]/(F_1,\ldots,F_m)$. It supplies Noetherian $A$ and a G-ring $A_{\mathfrak p}$, and identifies the given map with a local $R$-algebra map $\theta:B_{\mathfrak q}\to\widehat{A_{\mathfrak p}}$. Set $a_i=\theta(\overline T_i/1)$; the equations $F_j(a)=0$ follow by applying this ring map to the defining relations of $B$.

source.place: Tag 0CAU, lemma-map-approximation, statement and proof at lines 11017–11068; Artin approximation input is Smoothing Ring Maps Tag 0CAR, lemma-approximation-property-variant.

proof.text: View the $F_j$ as polynomials over $A$. Apply [lem-trf-artin-approximation-etale-local-map] with the Noetherian ring $A$, prime $\mathfrak p$, G-ring $A_{\mathfrak p}$, solution $(a_i)$, and the prescribed $N\geq1$. Obtain an étale $h:A\to A\prime$, a prime $\mathfrak p\prime$ over $\mathfrak p$, an isomorphism $\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to\kappa(\mathfrak p\prime)$, and a solution $(b_i)$ in $A\prime$ congruent to $(a_i)$ in $\widehat{A\prime_{\mathfrak p\prime}}$ modulo $J=(\mathfrak p\prime A\prime_{\mathfrak p\prime})^N\widehat{A\prime_{\mathfrak p\prime}}$. The affine chart dictionary also supplies Noetherianity of $A\prime$.

source.place: Tag 0CAU, lemma-map-approximation, statement and proof at lines 11017–11068; Artin approximation input is Smoothing Ring Maps Tag 0CAR, lemma-approximation-property-variant.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-generator-congruence-localization] to this presentation, $h$, the marked primes, $\theta$ and $(b_i)$. Its $R$-algebra map $\phi:B\to A\prime$ satisfies $\phi^{-1}(\mathfrak p\prime)=\mathfrak q$, and its localized map $\phi_{\mathfrak q}$ satisfies $\widehat h_{\mathfrak p}(\theta(z))-\iota(\phi_{\mathfrak q}(z))\in J$ for every $z\in B_{\mathfrak q}$, including fractions.

source.place: Tag 0CAU, lemma-map-approximation, statement and proof at lines 11017–11068; Artin approximation input is Smoothing Ring Maps Tag 0CAR, lemma-approximation-property-variant.

proof.text: Use the output part of [lem-trf-local-map-affine-chart-dictionary] with $h$ and $\phi$. It gives $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\prime$, $u=\mathfrak p\prime$, an étale $p_U:U\to X$ with unchanged residue field at $u$, and an $S$-morphism $f_U:U\to Y$ taking $u$ to $y$. Its identifications of stalk maps, induced completion maps, and extended maximal-ideal powers turn the preceding congruence into precisely the stated congruence for every $a\in\mathcal O_{Y,y}$. These are the required witnesses for the arbitrary $N$.
